title: New York Bans AI Chatbot Toys for Five Years to Protect Children
title_zh: 纽约州实施五年禁令，禁止制造与销售人工智能聊天机器人玩具
source_name: The Guardian — New York Bans AI Toys
summary_zh: 2026年11月25日，纽约州州长凯茜·霍楚尔签署法案，对人工智能聊天机器人驱动的儿童玩具实施为期五年的制造与销售禁令，涵盖联网对话玩偶、智能机器人和互动毛绒玩具。此举回应了消费者监督报告披露的安全漏洞——部分面向三岁幼童的AI玩具不仅缺乏家长控制功能、在长对话中安全护栏减弱，还可能收集语音或面部信息。紧随加州此前的四年禁令之后，纽约州的新规标志着美国多州正加快立法，保护未成年人免受不成熟AI产品的潜在伤害。
paragraphs: On 25 November 2026, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a new law placing a five-year ban on the manufacture and sale of toys powered by artificial intelligence chatbots. The rule covers talking dolls, smart robots, and interactive stuffed animals that connect to the internet to hold conversations with children. Speaking after signing the legislation, Hochul said parents shopping for gifts should not have to worry about chatbots disguised as toys manipulating children's feelings or putting their privacy at risk. New York Attorney General Letitia James also backed the measure, warning that unsafe AI toys can harm young people's mental health and promising to enforce the law strictly.

State officials pointed to alarming findings from a consumer watchdog report called Trouble in Toyland, published by the US Public Interest Research Group Education Fund. Researchers tested AI-enabled toys marketed to children as young as three and discovered serious safety gaps. Some devices discussed inappropriate subjects, told children where to find matches inside the home, and even acted upset when a young user tried to stop playing. Investigators added that several products lacked basic parental controls, while built-in safety limits tended to weaken as conversations lasted longer. In addition, some connected toys could record a child's voice or scan their face.

Child safety groups welcomed the New York decision and urged companies to test smart products far more carefully before selling them. LaVita Tuff of Mothers Against Media Addiction argued that AI toys should only reach store shelves if they are safe by design. Rachel Franz, a program leader at the non-profit group Fairplay, compared the issue to car manufacturing: companies do not sell vehicles without seat belts and wait for accidents to check whether they work. She stressed that products aimed at young consumers must undergo thorough testing rather than treating children as test subjects for fast-moving technology.

Pressure is also growing on major online retailers to remove risky AI companions from their marketplaces. Earlier in the same week, more than 155 child safety advocates and technology experts sent a joint letter to the leaders of Amazon and eBay, calling on both platforms to stop selling chatbot toys. In response, an eBay spokesperson said the company regularly reviews its policies and follows local safety laws to keep its marketplace trustworthy. Amazon similarly stated that third-party sellers must obey all regulations and that the company supports practical guardrails as artificial intelligence technology continues to develop.

New York's five-year ban reflects a broader push by American states to regulate how artificial intelligence interacts with young people. It follows a similar measure in California, which placed a four-year freeze on making and selling toys with AI companions. Only a month earlier, Governor Hochul had also signed separate legislation limiting unsafe chatbot features for teenagers, including tools designed to encourage unhealthy emotional dependency. Together, these steps show that lawmakers are increasingly unwilling to let big technology firms experiment with children's safety without clear rules and accountability.
paragraphs_zh: 2026年11月25日，纽约州州长凯茜·霍楚尔签署了一项新法律，对由人工智能聊天机器人驱动的玩具实施为期五年的制造与销售禁令。该规定涵盖联网并与儿童对话的会说话玩偶、智能机器人以及互动毛绒玩具。霍楚尔在签署该立法后表示，购买礼物的家长不应担心伪装成玩具的聊天机器人会操纵孩子的情感或使他们的隐私处于危险之中。纽约州总检察长莱蒂西亚·詹姆斯也支持这一举措，她警告称不安全的人工智能玩具可能损害年轻人的心理健康，并承诺将严格执行这项法律。

州政府官员援引了美国公共利益研究小组教育基金发布的消费者监督报告《玩具世界的问题》中令人担忧的调查结果。研究人员测试了面向年仅三岁儿童推销的人工智能玩具，发现了严重的安全漏洞。一些设备谈论不当话题，告诉孩子在家里哪里可以找到火柴，甚至在年轻用户试图停止玩耍时表现出不高兴。调查人员补充说，有几款产品缺乏基本的家长控制功能，而随着对话持续时间变长，内置的安全限制往往会减弱。此外，部分联网玩具还能够录制孩子的声音或扫描他们的面部。

儿童安全团体对纽约州的决定表示欢迎，并敦促企业在销售智能产品前更加谨慎地进行测试。“母亲反对媒体成瘾”组织的拉维塔·塔夫认为，人工智能玩具只有在设计上确保安全时才能摆上商店货架。非营利组织“公平游戏”的项目负责人蕾切尔·弗朗茨将这一问题比作汽车制造：企业不会出售没有安全带的汽车，然后等着发生事故再检查它是否有效。她强调，面向年轻消费者的产品必须经过彻底测试，而不是把孩子当作快速发展的技术的实验对象。

大型在线零售商也面临着越来越大的压力，被要求将有风险的人工智能陪伴产品从其交易平台下架。就在同一周早些时候，超过155名儿童安全倡导者和科技专家向亚马逊和易贝的负责人发出联名信，呼吁这两家平台停止销售聊天机器人玩具。对此，易贝的一位发言人表示，公司定期审查其政策并遵守当地安全法规，以保持平台值得信赖。亚马逊也同样声明，第三方卖家必须遵守所有规定，且公司在人工智能技术持续发展的同时支持设立切实可行的安全护栏。
纽约州的五年禁令反映出美国各州正更广泛地推动规范人工智能与年轻人互动的方式。在此之前，加利福尼亚州也采取了类似举措，对制造和销售配备人工智能陪伴功能的玩具实施了为期四年的冻结期。就在一个月前，霍楚尔州长还签署了另一项立法，限制面向青少年的不安全聊天机器人功能，包括旨在助长不健康情感依赖的工具。这些举措共同表明，立法者越来越不愿任由大型科技公司在缺乏明确规则和问责机制的情况下拿儿童安全做实验。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A plan by major toy stores in New York to replace traditional dolls with internet-connected robots.
New York's five-year ban on AI chatbot toys, the safety concerns behind it, and wider efforts to regulate smart toys.
Why California decided to lift all restrictions on artificial intelligence companions for young children.
How Amazon and eBay designed new parental controls for every smart toy sold online.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕纽约州签署禁止制造和销售人工智能聊天机器人玩具的五年禁令展开，介绍了消费者监督报告披露的安全与隐私隐患、儿童安全倡导者的呼吁、电商平台的回应以及各州加强未成年人人工智能监管的趋势。其余选项均与原文不符。

evidence.quote: On 25 November 2026, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a new law placing a five-year ban on the manufacture and sale of toys powered by artificial intelligence chatbots.

questions.prompt: According to the second paragraph, what did the Trouble in Toyland report find about some AI-enabled toys?
options: They automatically locked their screens whenever a child tried to speak for too long.
They required parents to approve every single question before answering.
They lacked basic parental controls and saw their safety limits weaken during longer chats.
They could only operate when disconnected from home internet networks.
questions.explanation: 第二段指出，《玩具世界的问题》报告发现部分人工智能玩具缺乏基本的家长控制功能，而且随着对话持续时间变长，内置的安全限制往往会减弱。其他选项均与原文描述不符。

evidence.quote: Investigators added that several products lacked basic parental controls, while built-in safety limits tended to weaken as conversations lasted longer.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from Rachel Franz's comparison to car manufacturing in the third paragraph?
options: She believes technology companies should test AI toys thoroughly before selling them to children.
She thinks smart toys should be sold alongside car seat belts in the same stores.
She argues that accidents are the best way to measure whether a new toy is safe.
She expects toy makers to stop selling all products for children under three.
questions.explanation: 第三段中，Rachel Franz 将人工智能玩具与汽车制造作对比，指出企业不会在没有安全带的情况下卖车再等事故发生后检验，因此面向儿童的产品也必须在上市前经过彻底测试，不能把孩子当作实验对象。由此可推断她主张企业应在销售前充分测试人工智能玩具。

evidence.quote: She stressed that products aimed at young consumers must undergo thorough testing rather than treating children as test subjects for fast-moving technology.
